newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Dewan Salman gains 13.93 pct.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Dewan Salman gains 13.93 pct.

text.p: Pakistan's Dewan Salman Fibre jumped 4.15 rupees, or 13.93 percent, to 33.95 on Thursday on the back of an expected increase in polyester staple fibre (PSF) prices in November, dealers said.
Some 2.5795 million shares of Dewan Salman had changed hands at the Karachi bourse by noon. Dealer Khalid Hussain said many synthetic fibre shares had risen on an expected PSF price rise.

ING Baring Securities said in its daily market preview that synthetic companies, which fix prices every month, were expected to raise PSF rates to 80 rupees per kg from 72 rupees to bring prices in line with PSF imports made costlier by last week's 7.86 percent devaluation of the rupee against the dollar.

Taurus Securities said in its review the gains were temporary. "We believe that local producers will find it difficult to maintain a higher gross margin when all the upcoming capacities will come on line," it said.
"Excess local supply from the beginning of '97 will force local PSF manufacturers to cut down capacity utilisation," it said, adding that price wars were a possibility.
